resolvedThisWave.name: Stalker
resolvedThisWave.edition: Silent Hill (1999), armed Nowhere Stalker; original CLD2 model
resolvedThisWave.resolution: One complete original-source-specific CLD2 Stalker, strict right-facing profile, egg-shaped bent-forward head, long arms, two hands, two legs, both whole blunt feet at a shared baseline, one low triangular knife. Body geometry traced to independent original CLD2, not Grey Child. Built-in imagegen correction gives genuine internal semi-transparency; subject alpha max213. Original RGBA bytes retained. Background, halo RGB under alpha0 and low-alpha speckles are excluded by actual compositing.
resolvedThisWave.limits: One newly authored static idle; no source animation, exact timing, original PlayStation subtractive blend or 1:1 fidelity certification. Whole geometry was established from original ILM/ANM/TIM documentary renders. Neutral archive renders do not reproduce final engine materials; Lost Memories commentary and released capture establish Nowhere shadow manifestation. Source pose is adapted to two grounded feet. Mirrored runtime presentation is authored, not a separately verified opposite-side source. Very low-alpha fringe remains; see raster QA. Root runtime visual QA required.

resolvedThisWave.name: Creeper Swarm — Film
resolvedThisWave.edition: Silent Hill (2006), Mr. X final creature design; three-member representative swarm presentation
resolvedThisWave.resolution: One collective image contains exactly three distinct complete right-facing insect profiles. Three separated alpha32 column groups corroborate the visual count. Each has a low segmented carapace, tapered rear tail, jointed legs and small human-like face integrated beneath the anterior shell; no separate human body is invented. The outer legs and all tails remain within the image. A few far legs are naturally occluded by near legs. The three support lines differ by only three native pixels. The result retains the earlier prototype count of three while explicitly treating it as a representative sample, not a canonical swarm size.
resolvedThisWave.limits: The source mesh is a production side-view sample and the construction prop predates final facial detailing; the final-film ventral close-up controls that detail. Generated surfaces, the opposite side, leg offsets and face projection remain reconstructions. The prompt requested 8 percent border; the nearest readable alpha8 silhouette is 28 pixels from the left edge (1.29 percent of native width), so the requested horizontal margin is not met, although no readable appendage is cut. Low-alpha native noise touches canvas edges and is preserved. The sprite is wide because all three complete insects share one support line. The proposed bodyHeight is a standing-equivalent presentation calibration to keep the collective footprint usable, not a measured source height. One actor profile, one static idle, no independent swarm actors, no source motion/cadence claim and no 1:1 certification. Root must inspect gameplay placement and scale.

resolvedThisWave.name: The Collector
resolvedThisWave.edition: Silent Hill: Ascension, released Chapter21 / scene177F
resolvedThisWave.resolution: Whole calm right-facing Collector with closed interlocking chest, finger-crown, long doubled forearms, slatted shoulder/hip plates, seal, divided heavy mantle, wrapped shins, feet and held crescent staff. Native imagegen correction lifts only lowest cape ends to sole/staff baseline; no floor or second figure. Both complete external contour and actual RGBA transparency verified.
resolvedThisWave.limits: One newly authored static side presentation; no canonical animation, opposite-side anatomy, exact staff ornament geometry, source timing or fidelity1:1 certification. Source colors in the episode are amber-lit; artist says sculpt textures unfinished. Corpus portal behavior is retained unchanged; this image depicts closed resting torso seen in final scene. Margins are smaller than the prompt asks (staff near y50) but all solid tips remain in frame. Tiny alpha1 fringe exists around the opaque silhouette; see exact alpha8/32 bounds. Further runtime visual QA is required before acceptance.
